channel.title: Nature Communications
channel.description:
Nature Communications is an open access, multidisciplinary journal dedicated to publishing high-quality research in all areas of the biological, health, physical, chemical and Earth sciences. Papers published by the journal aim to represent important advances of significance to specialists within each field.

We are committed to providing an efficient service for both authors and readers. Our team of independent editors make rapid and fair publication decisions. Prompt dissemination of accepted papers to a wide readership and beyond is achieved through a programme of continuous online publication.

item.title: Emergent memory in cell-like active systems
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77681-z

Living cells can exhibit complex, multi-timescale memory effects influencing their motility and responses to environmental cues. Here, the authors introduce a minimal theoretical framework demonstrating that when active particles, modeled after cells, incorporate internal state dynamics and environmental sensing, emergent environmental memory spontaneously arises.
item.dc:title: Emergent memory in cell-like active systems
item.dc:creator: M. Besse
R. Voituriez

item.title: Cryo-EM structures of autoinhibited and RNA-activated ZNFX1 helicase
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78145-0

ZNFX1 is an RNA helicase that plays a critical role in host defense against viral infections. Here, the authors reveal how RNA binding remodels autoinhibited ZNFX1 assemblies and activates the helicase for ATP-dependent RNA unwinding.
item.dc:title: Cryo-EM structures of autoinhibited and RNA-activated ZNFX1 helicase
item.dc:creator: Qing He

item.title: Distinct inflammatory marker profiles of adolescents and young adults among the HIV risk, infection, and treatment spectrum
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78034-6

Nielsen-Saines and colleagues identify unique and divergent immune perturbations across groups of youth living with or at risk of HIV. Their findings shed light on conserved and stage-specific that may underlie variations in outcomes and treatment success for HIV.

item.title: Holistic co-design of fibre-optic distributed acoustic sensing and coherent communication
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78056-0

Integrating sensing into communication is crucial for future fully-connected and intelligent networks. Here, authors develop a holistically co-designed fiber sensing and communication framework that shares signal, hardware, and network resources, supporting dense communication and diverse sensing.

item.title: Pathway to optical-cycle dynamic photonics: extreme electron temperatures in transparent conducting oxides
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77671-1

Controlling light-matter interactions within a few optical cycles could unlock new regimes of photonics. Here, authors show that extreme electron heating in transparent conducting oxides drives oscillatory optical responses and could enable refractive index modulation on optical-cycle timescales.

item.title: Topological memory of nonreciprocal scattering singularities
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77640-8

Wave systems with memory can exhibit topological effects that depend on their history. Here, the authors demonstrate hysteresis-driven topological memory in a nonreciprocal microwave system, linking scattering zeros to exceptional points and preserving them over long distances.
item.dc:title: Topological memory of nonreciprocal scattering singularities

item.title: A cross-species atlas platform for comparative neuroscience in teleost fish
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77879-1

This presents a scalable interactive brain atlas, which enables quantitative comparison of anatomical, molecular and functional data across zebrafish and medaka larvae, revealing both conserved and divergent features of brain organization and social processing.
item.dc:title: A cross-species atlas platform for comparative neuroscience in teleost fish
